source.title: Epoch wise critical periods, and singular learning theory

record.file_problem: None; the full post text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The post investigates epoch-wise critical periods under a blurred-to-sharp data shift. It does not test any of the listed double-descent versions; its mention of epoch-wise double descent is speculative and proposed as future work.
record.gate_note: The reported findings concern how the timing of a blurred-to-sharp training-data transition affects final CIFAR-10 accuracy, and how batch size changes the reported kink. They do not measure a fall-rise-fall test-error curve over epochs. The post also reports a qualitative relationship between estimated learning coefficients and the critical point, but not a double-descent peak.
record.test_reason: The post studies critical learning periods under a blurred-to-sharp CIFAR-10 data shift and how batch size moves the critical point. It reports no fall-rise-fall test-error curve along size, epochs or samples. It mentions epoch-wise double descent only as speculative future work, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors frame the results as consistent with a temperature/SGD-as-sampler account of critical periods: decreasing batch size pushed the critical point later. They say lambda-hat was only loosely informative, although the abstract claims the RLCT increased only during critical epochs. They state that epoch-wise double descent might be modulated by beta, implying a batch-size double descent; this is speculation, not a result.
record.recipe_differences: The post says it replicated a study of critical learning periods and added batch-size comparisons and learning-coefficient tracking; it does not apply a double-descent recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported critical-period timing differed with batch size: batch size 64 had a later kink than 128, while the kink for 256 was less obvious and did not increase.

fits_no_version.finding: In a blurred-to-sharp CIFAR-10 schedule, the critical-period kink falls between epochs 80 and 100 at batch size 128, and between 120 and 160 at batch size 64. At batch size 256 the kink is less clear but did not move later.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Smaller batch size delays the end of epoch-wise critical learning periods.

fits_no_version.finding: The estimated learning coefficient (lambda-hat) was only loosely informative about where the critical point lies. The abstract nonetheless claims it rises only during critical epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The estimated learning coefficient tracks critical-period transitions.

record.problems: Accuracy results are described qualitatively and through plots rather than with numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The author says the learning-coefficient estimates were only loosely informative, notes that the batch-size-256 kink is less obvious, and treats the theoretical account as provisional.
record.rows_left_out: No separately quantified learning-coefficient results were reported in the text; the qualitative overall statement is recorded in r4.

record.verdict_notes: An informal LessWrong post (a MATS application). It reports no numeric uncertainty, and the single runs per batch size are shown only as plots. It has no bearing on any double-descent version.

versions.untested_parts: Model-wise test error as model size grows, including a peak near interpolation.
Fall-rise-fall test error over training epochs.
